gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ midnight when we finally arrived.
gaps.explanation: 'Nearly' means almost; 'near' as a preposition needs a place object and cannot modify 'midnight'.

gaps.sentence: We ___ all major credit cards at the box office.
gaps.explanation: 'Accept' means to take or agree to something offered; 'except' means not including.

gaps.sentence: She is ___ of hearing after years beside the speakers.
gaps.explanation: 'Hard of hearing' is the fixed phrase; 'hardly' is an adverb.

gaps.sentence: Should any dispute ___, the matter will go to arbitration.
gaps.explanation: 'Arise' = (problems, disputes) occur; 'rise' means go up and 'raise' needs an object.

gaps.sentence: Do you know ___ bag this is?
I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: He should be ___ of himself for lying to his friends.
gaps.hint: feeling guilt about something you did; pattern: ___ of
gaps.explanation: 'Ashamed of' means feeling guilt or shame about behaviour; 'embarrassed' is only social discomfort.
